questions.q: Why does the lesson name colours by role (--surface, --ink) instead of by value (--white, --navy)?
questions.explain: --white that turns navy in dark mode is a lie in the stylesheet. --surface is "a card" in both themes, so a rule written once stays correct when the dark block gives it a new value.
options: Role names are shorter to type
A role keeps its meaning when its value changes, so the dark theme redefines the token and no rule has to change
Browsers only allow custom properties with role names
Value names cannot be used inside var()

questions.q: Ada swapped every black for white and every white for black, and the muted grey hint text became unreadable in dark mode. What went wrong?
questions.explain: The lesson lifts the muted grey in dark mode rather than inverting it, and keeps body text at 4.5:1 or better on both surfaces. Arithmetic on colours is not a substitute for checking the ratio.
options: Grey cannot be used on dark backgrounds
Contrast is not symmetric: the mirror of a grey that passes on white does not necessarily pass on a dark surface, so dark values must be chosen by measuring
She forgot to invert the grey
The browser caches the old colours

questions.q: After the tokens are declared, what does switching the whole page to dark require?
questions.explain: document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark") is the whole switch. The :root[data-theme="dark"] block redefines the tokens, and the rules that use var() do not know anything happened.
options: Re-running every rule with a class on each element
Loading a second stylesheet
Changing one attribute on the root element; every rule that reads a token picks up the new value
Calling getComputedStyle on every element

questions.q: Why does the lesson keep the preference ("system", "light", "dark") separate from the resolved theme ("light", "dark")?
questions.explain: A visitor on "system" sees dark at night and light by day without touching anything. Storing the resolved theme would freeze that; storing the preference keeps the OS in the loop.
options: Because localStorage can only store two values
"System" is a real choice that means "follow the OS", so what the visitor asked for and what is on screen are different questions with different answers
Because CSS cannot read a three-valued attribute
To make the toggle button larger

questions.q: resolveTheme("banana", false) returns "light". Why is that the right result?
questions.explain: The safe default for a preference nobody recognises is the OS answer. With the OS not preferring dark, that is light.
options: "banana" sorts alphabetically before "dark"
Anything that is not exactly "dark" or "light" means "follow the OS", so a corrupted or unknown stored value can never trap someone in a theme they did not choose
The function throws and the browser catches it
It is a bug the lesson asks you to fix

questions.q: Why does writePreference(storage, "system") remove the key instead of storing the string "system"?
questions.explain: Storing only explicit choices keeps the meaning of "nothing stored" clear, and it means the boot script's default (follow the OS) and the visitor's choice of "system" are the same state.
options: Strings longer than five characters are not allowed in localStorage
"System" is the absence of a choice: with nothing stored, a visitor who never touched the toggle keeps following the OS, and clearing the value is how you go back to that
Removing keys is faster than setting them
The storage event does not fire for the value "system"

questions.q: Ada's page is painted light for a moment and then goes dark on every reload. Where must the code that sets the theme attribute run to stop the flash?
questions.explain: The browser will not paint until the stylesheet has arrived, so an inline script placed above the stylesheet is guaranteed to run before the first paint. Anything deferred runs after it.
options: In a script at the bottom of <body> with defer
In a DOMContentLoaded handler
Inline in <head>, before the stylesheet <link>, so it runs before the first paint
In a service worker

questions.q: The boot script reads localStorage inside try … catch even though the catch block does nothing. Why?
questions.explain: The boot script must never throw. If storage is unavailable, the catch leaves saved as null, which resolves to the OS answer, and the page is still themed correctly.
options: To make the script run faster
Storage can throw in a private window or when site data is blocked, and an uncaught error in the boot script would leave the page unthemed on every visit
Because getItem returns a promise
It is required syntax for inline scripts

questions.q: Tab A changes the theme to dark. What does Tab B, open on the same site, receive?
questions.explain: The storage event fires in every other tab of the same origin when localStorage changes. The tab that made the change does not receive it, because it already knows. A key of null means the other tab cleared everything.
options: Nothing: tabs cannot communicate
A change event from matchMedia
A storage event on window with the key and the new value, because another tab wrote to localStorage
A page reload

questions.q: The code editor on this site switches its own colour scheme when the site theme changes. How does the theme module tell it, without knowing the editor exists?
questions.explain: One event, any number of listeners. The theme module has one job and never imports the editor, the chart or anything else that happens to care.
options: It calls editor.setTheme directly
It dispatches a CustomEvent on document with the details; the editor listens for that event
It reloads the page
It writes the theme into the editor's localStorage key

questions.q: What does color-scheme: dark on the root element change?
questions.explain: color-scheme tells the browser which theme the page is, so its built-in widgets match. Your tokens are still yours to define.
options: It sets every token to its dark value automatically
The browser's own parts: scrollbars, form controls and the default focus ring render in their dark style
It switches the page's images to dark versions
Nothing unless a media query also matches

questions.q: In the lesson's stylesheet the dark block does not redefine --accent. What is the effect?
questions.explain: A custom property resolves to the nearest declaration that applies. The dark block only overrides what it declares; everything else keeps the value from :root.
options: The accent becomes transparent in dark mode
The accent keeps its light value in both themes, because a token that is not redefined falls through to the :root declaration
The browser reports an error for the missing declaration
The accent inherits the text colour

questions.q: Why is a defer script the wrong place to set the theme attribute?
questions.explain: The first paint happens once the blocking stylesheet is in; deferred scripts run later. The boot block goes inline in <head>, above the stylesheet, precisely because inline scripts block parsing.
options: Deferred scripts cannot access document.documentElement
Deferred scripts run after the document is parsed, which is after the first paint, so the page shows the default theme first
Deferred scripts run before the stylesheet loads and the attribute is lost
Deferred scripts run in a Web Worker

questions.q: The OS switches to dark at sunset. Which event tells the page, and what should the page do if the visitor explicitly chose light?
questions.explain: A visitor who chose light stays light at sunset. The change listener checks the stored preference and only re-applies when it is "system".
options: resize on window; switch to dark anyway
change on the MediaQueryList from matchMedia; do nothing, because only a "system" preference follows the OS
storage on window; reload the page
DOMContentLoaded; ask the visitor again

questions.q: Tab A calls localStorage.setItem("theme", "dark"). Does Tab A itself receive a storage event?
questions.explain: The storage event exists to tell other documents. The tab that wrote the value updates itself directly.
options: Yes, every tab including the writer
No, only the other tabs of the same origin receive it; the writer already knows what it did
Only if Tab A is focused
Only for keys longer than 8 characters

questions.q: A storage event arrives with event.key === null. What happened?
questions.explain: A null key means the whole storage was cleared. The lesson's handler treats it like "our value is gone" and re-applies "system".
options: The other tab wrote an empty string
The other tab called localStorage.clear(), so every key, including ours, may be gone
The other tab closed
The event was dispatched by the browser on startup

questions.q: Because the boot script resolves "system" itself and always sets data-theme to "light" or "dark", what does the CSS need?
questions.explain: Resolving in one place avoids two copies of the dark tokens that could drift apart. The trade-off is that without JavaScript the page is always light, which the lesson accepts.
options: Two dark blocks: one for the attribute and one inside a prefers-color-scheme media query
One dark block keyed on the attribute; the media query is only consulted in JavaScript
A light block inside a media query
No dark block, because the attribute carries the colours

questions.q: Which of these is the theme module allowed to know about?
questions.explain: The theme module has one job and one event. Listeners come and go without the module changing.
options: The code editor's setTheme method
Every chart on the page
None of them: it dispatches one CustomEvent and the editor and charts listen
Only components registered in a global list

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: "light" wins over the OS. undefined is not "dark" or "light", so it follows the OS (dark). "DARK" in capitals is not exactly "dark", so it also follows the OS, which here is light.
options: light dark dark
light dark light
dark dark dark
light light light

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: "dark" is the last entry, so the remainder wraps to index 0, "system". An unknown value gives indexOf of -1, and (-1 + 1) % 3 is 0, "system" again.
options: light system light
light dark light
light system system
light undefined undefined

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The stored value is "dark " with a trailing space, which is not exactly "dark", so it means "system". The broken storage throws and the catch returns "system". The third storage returns exactly "light".
options: dark system light
system system light
dark  system light
system light light

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Writing "dark" stores it; writing "system" removes the key rather than storing the word, so the map ends empty.
options: 1 true
0 false
1 false
2 true

questions.q: What does this print? (EventTarget and CustomEvent exist in Node.js and the browser.)
questions.explain: Listeners run in the order they were added, and each reads what it asked for from detail.
options:
A system
B dark

A dark
B system

B system
A dark
A dark

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: This is the same fall-through as the CSS: the dark set only overrides what it names, and the accent keeps the light value. Spreading merges by key, so there are still three keys.
options: #C0392B #FAFAF9 3
undefined #0F0F1A 2

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A stored "dark" or "light" wins outright; with nothing stored, the OS answer decides. This is the exact expression the boot block uses.
options: dark light dark light
dark dark dark light
dark light light light
light light dark light

questions.q: Write resolveTheme(preference, osPrefersDark): "dark" and "light" return themselves; anything else returns the OS answer.
questions.explain: Only the two exact strings are honoured. Everything else, including numbers and typos, follows the OS.

questions.q: Write nextPreference(current) that cycles through ["system", "light", "dark"], wrapping at the end, and returns "system" for any unknown value.
questions.explain: indexOf plus one, modulo the length, wraps the end to the start and sends unknown values (index -1) to the first entry.

questions.q: Write readPreference(storage) that returns the stored "light" or "dark" under the key "theme", and "system" for a missing value, any other value, or a storage that throws.
questions.explain: The read happens inside try, and every path that is not an exact "light" or "dark" ends in "system".

questions.q: Write writePreference(storage, preference): store "light" or "dark" under "theme", remove the key for anything else, and return true on success or false if the storage throws.
questions.explain: "System" is stored as the absence of a value. A throwing storage turns into false, never into a crash.

questions.q: Write announce(target, preference, resolved) that dispatches a CustomEvent named "theme:change" on target with { preference, resolved } as its detail.
questions.explain: The event carries its data in detail; listeners never need to know who dispatched it.
questions.expected:
theme:change system -> dark
theme:change light -> light

questions.q: Write themeValues(light, darkOverrides, theme) that returns the light token object for "light", and for "dark" the light object with the overrides applied on top, without changing either input.
questions.explain: Spreading builds a new object, so the light set is untouched, and a token the dark set does not name keeps its light value, exactly like the CSS.
